opportunity: decbench:arm-entry-granularity step 3 (PROPOSAL PR #239) — the tailcall sub-class
test_name: kuna-analysis entry recall, decbench ARM Cortex-M corpus (8 projects x 3 opt levels, 96 images, 43809 DWARF entries)
inspiration: decbench:O2-noinline-chibios-ch, O2-noinline-crazyflie-cf2, O2-nuttx-nuttx, O2-riot-os-hello-world, O0-crazyflie-CMSIS_DAP; kuna's own ARM entry-recall measurement (docs/features/arm-entry-granularity/, step 3). Recognition after angr CFGFast's job model, where a branch outside the current function's block set starts a new function; the precision model is kuna's own region containment, the mirror of ptrentry's same-function guard.

surface_listing_on_stacked_on_ptrentry.note: Exactly orthogonal to proposal step 2: identical delta with ptrentry off and on, because both emit additive entry facts and neither enters Listing::functions(), which is what the region-containment guard reads. Stacked corpus recall 97.2%.

surface_listing_off.note: tailcallentry is a Listing consumer; with the Listing off there is nothing to consume, so the surface is structurally inert on all 96 images.

rejected_arm_proposal_naive_tailcall_rul.note: The proposal's 39%/55% arm, re-measured on the full 96 images.

rejected_arm_proposal_stricter_rule.note: The proposal's 54%/38% arm; this is the shipped ImpurePredecessor guard on its own.

rejected_model_stack_discipline.note: Reject a branch taken with an unmatched PUSH/SUB SP/VPUSH/STMDB SP! still open (a forward may-analysis over the caller's region). Principled and dominated by region containment on precision AND on splits.

rejected_guard_alignment_padding.note: 1.6pp of precision, almost all of it in the unverifiable outside-any-DWARF-body bucket, for 186 ground-truth functions.

aif_gap_start_rewalk.note: Measured on this branch (reverted; not in this diff). The tail-call split does NOT make the re-seed safe — it makes it slightly worse. A split leaves the walk's decoded-instruction closure fixed; a re-seed adds to it, turning undefined gaps into code and making other stages' candidates fail their is_undefined guard. Needs its own investigation.

O2/u-boot (ARM Linux, A32).note: In scope (the gate is Architecture::Arm, the same one Stages 2 and 3 use). Clears the >=80% bar on a population the model was never fitted on (A32, not Thumb; Linux, not bare metal), but the 2 splits are outside the zero-split Cortex-M result. Both are 3-instruction regions inside a sparsely walked function; a length floor removes them and costs ~60 Cortex-M ground-truth entries, the trade step 2 rejected. Disclosed rather than gated away.

speed.samples: interleaved off/on pairs, minimum reported (shared box)
speed.note: The gzip row is a provable strict no-op (ARM-gated, byte-identical output), so -0.21% is the measurement floor. Every discovery-surface delta is inside it plus run-to-run noise. The decompile-all deltas are the extra decompile work for the extra functions and are sub-proportional to it (chibios +67 functions of 620 = +10.8% work for +1.92% wall clock); the negative rows are noise, since the option only ever adds functions.

catalog_counts.note: Derived from a fresh `phase catalog` capture on the rebased tree (origin/main 4c2b59bb, after #255 ptrentry and #257 undefname), not by arithmetic. The rebase produced a textbook instance of the stale-count trap: ptrentry and this row made the SAME edit to the same two count comments, so the conflict was real rather than silent, and both were resolved to base + both. `kuna catalog --check`, the kuna_phases count tests and catalog_bytecompat confirm.

notes: Default-OFF. No DIV row: default output is byte-identical. This is the step of the arm-entry-granularity sequence the proposal flagged as carrying the real precision risk (its naive arm split 55% of the time), so the acceptance table needs a human read before merge. The u-boot A32 result (2 splits) is the one disclosed non-zero-split number.
rebased_onto: origin/main 4c2b59bb (after #255 ptrentry, #257 undefname); the acceptance table re-measured on the rebased build is identical (593/561/0/32), and the per-binary entry sets differ in 0 of 96 images.
